1	"""Disposable end-to-end fixture for one real Claude Code lane on an Ollama backend.
2	
3	This fixture is the claude-code counterpart of ``disposable_coding_fixture.py``
4	but intentionally simpler: one Git worktree, one lane, the real ``claude`` CLI
5	as the provider binary.  It exercises the canonical
6	``orchestrator-worker-invocation/v1`` route for ``provider.id="claude-code"``.
7	
8	The fixture never sets ANTHROPIC_* process variables itself.  The ONLY
9	mechanism that redirects the provider child to the local Ollama
10	Anthropic-compatible endpoint is the invocation's ``provider.config_overrides``
11	channel: the ``model_provider="ollama"`` alias is translated by
12	``claude_config_override_env`` into ``ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`` /
13	``ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`` / ``ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`` child-environment entries that
14	the lane controller merges after any child-environment isolation.  If that
15	merge were broken, the claude child would attempt api.anthropic.com and fail
16	authentication.
17	
18	Run this file directly from the portable repository root:
19	    python examples/disposable_claude_coding_fixture.py [--keep DIRECTORY]
20	
21	The fixture passes when the real claude subprocess launches (PROVIDER_STARTED),
22	exits cleanly with a real session id, the provider terminal outcome is
23	COMPLETED, and the worktree contains the committed HELLO.txt artifact.
24	"""
25	
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import hashlib
29	import json
30	import os
31	import shutil
32	import subprocess
33	import sys
34	import tempfile
35	import time
36	from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
37	from pathlib import Path
38	from typing import Any
39	
40	# Direct execution puts ``examples/`` first on sys.path. Keep the documented
41	# root-level command equivalent to importing this fixture from its package.
42	HARNESS_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
43	if str(HARNESS_ROOT) not in sys.path:
44	    sys.path.insert(0, str(HARNESS_ROOT))
45	
46	from orchestrator_harness.models import iso_utc
47	from orchestrator_harness.processes import (
48	    WINDOWS_CREATE_NO_WINDOW,
49	    targeted_process_query,
50	)
51	from orchestrator_harness.prompt_bundle import prompt_bundle_record_from_paths
52	from orchestrator_harness.public_launch import launch_lane_controller
53	
54	# The real claude lane makes a real Ollama round-trip; bound it generously but
55	# keep the fixture finite.
56	FIXTURE_CONTROLLER_COMPLETION_SECONDS = 240
57	
58	# A real model served by the local Ollama (the endpoint the config_overrides
59	# channel redirects to).  Must be passed through provider.model so the claude
60	# CLI sends it as ``--model``.
61	CLAUDE_MODEL = "deepseek-v4-flash:0731-cloud"
62	
63	# The 0.3 config-overrides alias that expands (in claude_config_override_env)
64	# to ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=ollama,
65	# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="".  This is the ONLY redirect the fixture relies on.
66	CLAUDE_OLLAMA_OVERRIDE = 'model_provider="ollama"'
67	
68	
69	class FixtureError(RuntimeError):
70	    pass
71	
72	
73	def _run(
74	    argv: Sequence[str],
75	    *,
76	    cwd: Path,
77	    env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
78	    expected: tuple[int, ...] = (0,),
79	    timeout: float = 60,
80	) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
81	    completed = subprocess.run(
82	        list(argv),
83	        cwd=cwd,
84	        env=env,
85	        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
86	        capture_output=True,
87	        check=False,
88	        text=True,
89	        encoding="utf-8",
90	        errors="replace",
91	        timeout=timeout,
92	        shell=False,
93	        creationflags=WINDOWS_CREATE_NO_WINDOW if os.name == "nt" else 0,
94	    )
95	    if completed.returncode not in expected:
96	        raise FixtureError(
97	            f"command failed ({completed.returncode}): {list(argv)!r}\n"
98	            f"stdout: {completed.stdout[-2000:]}\nstderr: {completed.stderr[-2000:]}"
99	        )
100	    return completed
101	
102	
103	def _git(cwd: Path, *args: str) -> str:
104	    return _run(("git", *args), cwd=cwd).stdout.strip()
105	
106	
107	def _write_json(path: Path, value: object) -> None:
108	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
109	    path.write_text(
110	        json.dumps(value, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
111	    )
112	
113	
114	def _claude_command() -> list[str]:
115	    """Resolve the real Claude Code CLI exactly as a caller would on PATH."""
116	    claude = shutil.which("claude")
117	    if not claude:
118	        raise FixtureError("no claude CLI on PATH; install Claude Code")
119	    return [claude]
120	
121	
122	def _invocation(
123	    *,
124	    lane: str,
125	    worktree: Path,
126	    common_dir: Path,
127	    base_commit: str,
128	    runtime: Path,
129	    prompt_text: str,
130	    command: Sequence[str],
131	) -> Path:
132	    workspace = worktree / ".agent-workspace"
133	    workspace.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
134	    prompt = workspace / "worker-prompt.md"
135	    prompt.write_text(prompt_text, encoding="utf-8")
136	    branch = _git(worktree, "branch", "--show-current")
137	    worker_id = f"{lane}-001"
138	    card = {
139	        "schema": "orchestrator-task-card/v1",
140	        "card_id": f"card-{lane}",
141	        "lane_id": lane,
142	        "stage_cohort_id": "cohort-claude-fixture",
143	        "worker_invocation_id": worker_id,
144	        "objective": "Create HELLO.txt and commit it",
145	        "revision": "r1",
146	    }
147	    workflow_id = "disposable-claude-fixture"
148	    profile_id = f"profile-{lane}"
149	    tools = ["Read", "Bash", "Write", "Edit", "Glob", "Grep"]
150	    # Canonical lanes isolate the provider child environment by default.  The
151	    # provider_needs grants keep Claude's config/home resolvable under the
152	    # caller's control (set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR when launching the fixture); the
153	    # config_overrides channel below still supplies the ANTHROPIC_* redirect.
154	    profile = {
155	        "schema": "orchestrator-runtime-profile/v1",
156	        "id": profile_id,
157	        "role": "implementer",
158	        "provider": "claude-code",
159	        "model": CLAUDE_MODEL,
160	        "tools": tools,
161	        "capabilities": ["repo"],
162	        "resources": [],
163	        "provider_needs": ["CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR", "HOME"],
164	    }
165	    bundle = prompt_bundle_record_from_paths(
166	        workflow_id=workflow_id,
167	        task_card_id=card["card_id"],
168	        profile_id=profile_id,
169	        paths=(("instructions", prompt),),
170	        run_root=worktree,
171	    )
172	    invocation = {
173	        "schema": "orchestrator-worker-invocation/v1",
174	        "action": "start",
175	        "run_root": str(worktree),
176	        "runtime_root": str(runtime),
177	        "lane_id": lane,
178	        "worker_invocation_id": worker_id,
179	        "cohort_id": "cohort-claude-fixture",
180	        "workflow": {"id": workflow_id, "version": "1"},
181	        "task_card": {
182	            "id": card["card_id"],
183	            "revision": card["revision"],
184	            "sha256": hashlib.sha256(
185	                json.dumps(card, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode(
186	                    "utf-8"
187	                )
188	            ).hexdigest(),
189	        },
190	        "role": "implementer",
191	        "provider": {
192	            "id": "claude-code",
193	            "model": CLAUDE_MODEL,
194	            "command": list(command),
195	            "allowed_tools": tools,
196	            # The 0.3 child-env channel: the alias expands to ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
197	            # / ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and is merged into the
198	            # provider child environment AFTER isolation.  No service_tier or
199	            # approval_policy may appear here (both raise for claude-code).
200	            "config_overrides": [CLAUDE_OLLAMA_OVERRIDE],
201	        },
202	        "profile": profile,
203	        "prompt_bundle": bundle,
204	        "output_paths": {
205	            "status": str(workspace / "worker_controller.status.json"),
206	            "jsonl": str(workspace / "worker_claude.jsonl"),
207	            "stderr": str(workspace / "worker_claude.stderr.log"),
208	            "last_message": str(workspace / "worker_last_message.txt"),
209	        },
210	        "event_log_path": str(runtime / "LANE_EVENTS.jsonl"),
211	        "resources": [],
212	        "repository": {
213	            "common_dir": str(common_dir),
214	            "worktree_root": str(worktree),
215	            "branch": branch,
216	            "base_commit": base_commit,
217	        },
218	    }
219	    path = workspace / "invocation.json"
220	    _write_json(path, invocation)
221	    return path
222	
223	
224	def _start_controller(invocation: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
225	    """Use the same operator-launch -> lane-controller path as a manager."""
226	    raw = json.loads(invocation.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
227	    status_path = Path(raw["output_paths"]["status"])
228	    receipt_path = invocation.parent / "fixture_operator_launch.json"
229	    return launch_lane_controller(
230	        invocation,
231	        receipt=receipt_path,
232	        cwd=HARNESS_ROOT,
233	        expected_state_path=status_path,
234	    )
235	
236	
237	def _wait_for_status(
238	    path: Path,
239	    predicate: Any,
240	    *,
241	    timeout: float = FIXTURE_CONTROLLER_COMPLETION_SECONDS,
242	) -> dict[str, Any]:
243	    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
244	    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
245	        try:
246	            value = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
247	        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
248	            time.sleep(0.05)
249	            continue
250	        if isinstance(value, dict) and predicate(value):
251	            return value
252	        time.sleep(0.05)
253	    raise FixtureError(f"timed out waiting for status condition in {path}")
254	
255	
256	def _finish_controller(receipt: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
257	    """Wait for the canonical (non-legacy) lane to reach its terminal state.
258	
259	    A canonical invocation uses the provider-neutral state vocabulary:
260	    ``PROVIDER_EXITED`` is the terminal success state (the legacy coding-v1
261	    route calls it ``CODEX_EXITED``).  Discovered from lane_controller.py:
262	    ``exited_state = "CODEX_EXITED" if legacy_status_names else "PROVIDER_EXITED"``.
263	    """
264	    pid = receipt.get("pid")
265	    created_utc = receipt.get("created_utc")
266	    if not isinstance(pid, int) or not isinstance(created_utc, str):
267	        raise FixtureError(
268	            f"operator launch receipt has no exact process identity: {receipt}"
269	        )
270	    terminal_states = {
271	        "PROVIDER_EXITED",
272	        "CONTROLLER_FAILED",
273	        "LAUNCH_FAILED",
274	        "PROVIDER_HANDOFF",
275	        "PROVIDER_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED",
276	        "COORDINATION_FAILED",
277	    }
278	    deadline = time.monotonic() + FIXTURE_CONTROLLER_COMPLETION_SECONDS
279	    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
280	        query = targeted_process_query(pid)
281	        if query.complete and not query.errors:
282	            process = query.process
283	            if process is None or iso_utc(process.created_utc) != created_utc:
284	                status_path = Path(str(receipt["expected_state_path"]))
285	                return _wait_for_status(
286	                    status_path,
287	                    lambda value: value.get("state") in terminal_states,
288	                )
289	        time.sleep(0.05)
290	    raise FixtureError(
291	        f"controller PID {pid} with creation identity {created_utc} did not exit"
292	    )
293	
294	
295	def _lane_events(runtime: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
296	    path = runtime / "LANE_EVENTS.jsonl"
297	    rows = []
298	    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
299	        if line.strip():
300	            rows.append(json.loads(line))
301	    return rows
302	
303	
304	def run_fixture(root: Path) -> dict[str, object]:
305	    root = root.resolve()
306	    project = root / "project"
307	    worktrees = root / "worktrees"
308	    runtime = root / "runtime"
309	    project.mkdir(parents=True)
310	    worktrees.mkdir()
311	    runtime.mkdir()
312	    _git(project, "init", "-b", "main")
313	    _git(project, "config", "user.email", "fixture@example.invalid")
314	    _git(project, "config", "user.name", "Disposable Fixture")
315	    (project / "README.md").write_text("# Fixture project\n", encoding="utf-8")
316	    # Keep the controller workspace out of the model's commit scope.
317	    (project / ".gitignore").write_text(".agent-workspace/\n", encoding="utf-8")
318	    _git(project, "add", "README.md", ".gitignore")
319	    _git(project, "commit", "-m", "Initial fixture project")
320	    base_commit = _git(project, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
321	    common_dir = (project / ".git").resolve()
322	    lane = worktrees / "lane-claude"
323	    _git(project, "worktree", "add", "-b", "lane/claude-hello", str(lane), base_commit)
324	
325	    prompt_text = (
326	        "This is a disposable fixture task. Do exactly this:\n"
327	        "\n"
328	        "1. Create a file named HELLO.txt in the current directory whose\n"
329	        "   content is exactly this single line:\n"
330	        "\n"
331	        "   hello from claude\n"
332	        "\n"
333	        "2. Stage and commit it:\n"
334	        "\n"
335	        "   git add HELLO.txt\n"
336	        "   git commit -m \"add HELLO.txt\"\n"
337	        "\n"
338	        "Then reply with one short line containing the commit hash. Do not\n"
339	        "modify anything else and do not ask questions.\n"
340	    )
341	    invocation = _invocation(
342	        lane="claude-hello",
343	        worktree=lane,
344	        common_dir=common_dir,
345	        base_commit=base_commit,
346	        runtime=runtime,
347	        prompt_text=prompt_text,
348	        command=_claude_command(),
349	    )
350	
351	    receipt = _start_controller(invocation)
352	    status_path = lane / ".agent-workspace" / "worker_controller.status.json"
353	    status = _finish_controller(receipt)
354	
355	    if status.get("state") != "PROVIDER_EXITED":
356	        raise FixtureError(
357	            f"controller did not reach PROVIDER_EXITED; state={status.get('state')!r} "
358	            f"error={status.get('error')!r}"
359	        )
360	    if status.get("exit_code") != 0:
361	        raise FixtureError(
362	            f"provider exit code {status.get('exit_code')!r} is not 0; "
363	            f"stderr_path={status.get('stderr_path')!r}"
364	        )
365	    outcome = status.get("provider_terminal_outcome")
366	    if outcome != "COMPLETED":
367	        raise FixtureError(
368	            f"provider terminal outcome {outcome!r} is not COMPLETED"
369	        )
370	    session_id = status.get("provider_session_id")
371	    if not isinstance(session_id, str) or not session_id.strip():
372	        raise FixtureError(
373	            f"provider_session_id was not recorded: {session_id!r}"
374	        )
375	
376	    events = _lane_events(runtime)
377	    # Lane event rows carry the event name under ``event`` (see lane_controller
378	    # ``_event``), not ``type``; the claude stream-json lines use ``type``.
379	    event_types = [row.get("event") for row in events]

"""Disposable end-to-end fixture for one real Claude Code lane on an Ollama backend.

This fixture is the claude-code counterpart of ``disposable_coding_fixture.py``
but intentionally simpler: one Git worktree, one lane, the real ``claude`` CLI
as the provider binary.  It exercises the canonical
``orchestrator-worker-invocation/v1`` route for ``provider.id="claude-code"``.

The fixture never sets ANTHROPIC_* process variables itself.  The ONLY
mechanism that redirects the provider child to the local Ollama
Anthropic-compatible endpoint is the invocation's ``provider.config_overrides``
channel: the ``model_provider="ollama"`` alias is translated by
``claude_config_override_env`` into ``ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`` /
``ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`` / ``ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`` child-environment entries that
the lane controller merges after any child-environment isolation.  If that
merge were broken, the claude child would attempt api.anthropic.com and fail
authentication.

Run this file directly from the portable repository root:
    python examples/disposable_claude_coding_fixture.py [--keep DIRECTORY]

The fixture passes when the real claude subprocess launches (PROVIDER_STARTED),
exits cleanly with a real session id, the provider terminal outcome is
COMPLETED, and the worktree contains the committed HELLO.txt artifact.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

# Direct execution puts ``examples/`` first on sys.path. Keep the documented
# root-level command equivalent to importing this fixture from its package.
HARNESS_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
if str(HARNESS_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(HARNESS_ROOT))

from orchestrator_harness.models import iso_utc
from orchestrator_harness.processes import (
    WINDOWS_CREATE_NO_WINDOW,
    targeted_process_query,
)
from orchestrator_harness.prompt_bundle import prompt_bundle_record_from_paths
from orchestrator_harness.public_launch import launch_lane_controller

# The real claude lane makes a real Ollama round-trip; bound it generously but
# keep the fixture finite.
FIXTURE_CONTROLLER_COMPLETION_SECONDS = 240

# A real model served by the local Ollama (the endpoint the config_overrides
# channel redirects to).  Must be passed through provider.model so the claude
# CLI sends it as ``--model``.
CLAUDE_MODEL = "deepseek-v4-flash:0731-cloud"

# The 0.3 config-overrides alias that expands (in claude_config_override_env)
# to ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=ollama,
# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="".  This is the ONLY redirect the fixture relies on.
CLAUDE_OLLAMA_OVERRIDE = 'model_provider="ollama"'


class FixtureError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def _run(
    argv: Sequence[str],
    *,
    cwd: Path,
    env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    expected: tuple[int, ...] = (0,),
    timeout: float = 60,
) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    completed = subprocess.run(
        list(argv),
        cwd=cwd,
        env=env,
        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        capture_output=True,
        check=False,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        errors="replace",
        timeout=timeout,
        shell=False,
        creationflags=WINDOWS_CREATE_NO_WINDOW if os.name == "nt" else 0,
    )
    if completed.returncode not in expected:
        raise FixtureError(
            f"command failed ({completed.returncode}): {list(argv)!r}\n"
            f"stdout: {completed.stdout[-2000:]}\nstderr: {completed.stderr[-2000:]}"
        )
    return completed


def _git(cwd: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    return _run(("git", *args), cwd=cwd).stdout.strip()


def _write_json(path: Path, value: object) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(
        json.dumps(value, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )


def _claude_command() -> list[str]:
    """Resolve the real Claude Code CLI exactly as a caller would on PATH."""
    claude = shutil.which("claude")
    if not claude:
        raise FixtureError("no claude CLI on PATH; install Claude Code")
    return [claude]


def _invocation(
    *,
    lane: str,
    worktree: Path,
    common_dir: Path,
    base_commit: str,
    runtime: Path,
    prompt_text: str,
    command: Sequence[str],
) -> Path:
    workspace = worktree / ".agent-workspace"
    workspace.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    prompt = workspace / "worker-prompt.md"
    prompt.write_text(prompt_text, encoding="utf-8")
    branch = _git(worktree, "branch", "--show-current")
    worker_id = f"{lane}-001"
    card = {
        "schema": "orchestrator-task-card/v1",
        "card_id": f"card-{lane}",
        "lane_id": lane,
        "stage_cohort_id": "cohort-claude-fixture",
        "worker_invocation_id": worker_id,
        "objective": "Create HELLO.txt and commit it",
        "revision": "r1",
    }
    workflow_id = "disposable-claude-fixture"
    profile_id = f"profile-{lane}"
    tools = ["Read", "Bash", "Write", "Edit", "Glob", "Grep"]
    # Canonical lanes isolate the provider child environment by default.  The
    # provider_needs grants keep Claude's config/home resolvable under the
    # caller's control (set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR when launching the fixture); the
    # config_overrides channel below still supplies the ANTHROPIC_* redirect.
    profile = {
        "schema": "orchestrator-runtime-profile/v1",
        "id": profile_id,
        "role": "implementer",
        "provider": "claude-code",
        "model": CLAUDE_MODEL,
        "tools": tools,
        "capabilities": ["repo"],
        "resources": [],
        "provider_needs": ["CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR", "HOME"],
    }
    bundle = prompt_bundle_record_from_paths(
        workflow_id=workflow_id,
        task_card_id=card["card_id"],
        profile_id=profile_id,
        paths=(("instructions", prompt),),
        run_root=worktree,
    )
    invocation = {
        "schema": "orchestrator-worker-invocation/v1",
        "action": "start",
        "run_root": str(worktree),
        "runtime_root": str(runtime),
        "lane_id": lane,
        "worker_invocation_id": worker_id,
        "cohort_id": "cohort-claude-fixture",
        "workflow": {"id": workflow_id, "version": "1"},
        "task_card": {
            "id": card["card_id"],
            "revision": card["revision"],
            "sha256": hashlib.sha256(
                json.dumps(card, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode(
                    "utf-8"
                )
            ).hexdigest(),
        },
        "role": "implementer",
        "provider": {
            "id": "claude-code",
            "model": CLAUDE_MODEL,
            "command": list(command),
            "allowed_tools": tools,
            # The 0.3 child-env channel: the alias expands to ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
            # / ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and is merged into the
            # provider child environment AFTER isolation.  No service_tier or
            # approval_policy may appear here (both raise for claude-code).
            "config_overrides": [CLAUDE_OLLAMA_OVERRIDE],
        },
        "profile": profile,
        "prompt_bundle": bundle,
        "output_paths": {
            "status": str(workspace / "worker_controller.status.json"),
            "jsonl": str(workspace / "worker_claude.jsonl"),
            "stderr": str(workspace / "worker_claude.stderr.log"),
            "last_message": str(workspace / "worker_last_message.txt"),
        },
        "event_log_path": str(runtime / "LANE_EVENTS.jsonl"),
        "resources": [],
        "repository": {
            "common_dir": str(common_dir),
            "worktree_root": str(worktree),
            "branch": branch,
            "base_commit": base_commit,
        },
    }
    path = workspace / "invocation.json"
    _write_json(path, invocation)
    return path


def _start_controller(invocation: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Use the same operator-launch -> lane-controller path as a manager."""
    raw = json.loads(invocation.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    status_path = Path(raw["output_paths"]["status"])
    receipt_path = invocation.parent / "fixture_operator_launch.json"
    return launch_lane_controller(
        invocation,
        receipt=receipt_path,
        cwd=HARNESS_ROOT,
        expected_state_path=status_path,
    )


def _wait_for_status(
    path: Path,
    predicate: Any,
    *,
    timeout: float = FIXTURE_CONTROLLER_COMPLETION_SECONDS,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        try:
            value = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            time.sleep(0.05)
            continue
        if isinstance(value, dict) and predicate(value):
            return value
        time.sleep(0.05)
    raise FixtureError(f"timed out waiting for status condition in {path}")


def _finish_controller(receipt: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Wait for the canonical (non-legacy) lane to reach its terminal state.

    A canonical invocation uses the provider-neutral state vocabulary:
    ``PROVIDER_EXITED`` is the terminal success state (the legacy coding-v1
    route calls it ``CODEX_EXITED``).  Discovered from lane_controller.py:
    ``exited_state = "CODEX_EXITED" if legacy_status_names else "PROVIDER_EXITED"``.
    """
    pid = receipt.get("pid")
    created_utc = receipt.get("created_utc")
    if not isinstance(pid, int) or not isinstance(created_utc, str):
        raise FixtureError(
            f"operator launch receipt has no exact process identity: {receipt}"
        )
    terminal_states = {
        "PROVIDER_EXITED",
        "CONTROLLER_FAILED",
        "LAUNCH_FAILED",
        "PROVIDER_HANDOFF",
        "PROVIDER_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED",
        "COORDINATION_FAILED",
    }
    deadline = time.monotonic() + FIXTURE_CONTROLLER_COMPLETION_SECONDS
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        query = targeted_process_query(pid)
        if query.complete and not query.errors:
            process = query.process
            if process is None or iso_utc(process.created_utc) != created_utc:
                status_path = Path(str(receipt["expected_state_path"]))
                return _wait_for_status(
                    status_path,
                    lambda value: value.get("state") in terminal_states,
                )
        time.sleep(0.05)
    raise FixtureError(
        f"controller PID {pid} with creation identity {created_utc} did not exit"
    )


def _lane_events(runtime: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    path = runtime / "LANE_EVENTS.jsonl"
    rows = []
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if line.strip():
            rows.append(json.loads(line))
    return rows


def run_fixture(root: Path) -> dict[str, object]:
    root = root.resolve()
    project = root / "project"
    worktrees = root / "worktrees"
    runtime = root / "runtime"
    project.mkdir(parents=True)
    worktrees.mkdir()
    runtime.mkdir()
    _git(project, "init", "-b", "main")
    _git(project, "config", "user.email", "fixture@example.invalid")
    _git(project, "config", "user.name", "Disposable Fixture")
    (project / "README.md").write_text("# Fixture project\n", encoding="utf-8")
    # Keep the controller workspace out of the model's commit scope.
    (project / ".gitignore").write_text(".agent-workspace/\n", encoding="utf-8")
    _git(project, "add", "README.md", ".gitignore")
    _git(project, "commit", "-m", "Initial fixture project")
    base_commit = _git(project, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
    common_dir = (project / ".git").resolve()
    lane = worktrees / "lane-claude"
    _git(project, "worktree", "add", "-b", "lane/claude-hello", str(lane), base_commit)

    prompt_text = (
        "This is a disposable fixture task. Do exactly this:\n"
        "\n"
        "1. Create a file named HELLO.txt in the current directory whose\n"
        "   content is exactly this single line:\n"
        "\n"
        "   hello from claude\n"
        "\n"
        "2. Stage and commit it:\n"
        "\n"
        "   git add HELLO.txt\n"
        "   git commit -m \"add HELLO.txt\"\n"
        "\n"
        "Then reply with one short line containing the commit hash. Do not\n"
        "modify anything else and do not ask questions.\n"
    )
    invocation = _invocation(
        lane="claude-hello",
        worktree=lane,
        common_dir=common_dir,
        base_commit=base_commit,
        runtime=runtime,
        prompt_text=prompt_text,
        command=_claude_command(),
    )

    receipt = _start_controller(invocation)
    status_path = lane / ".agent-workspace" / "worker_controller.status.json"
    status = _finish_controller(receipt)

    if status.get("state") != "PROVIDER_EXITED":
        raise FixtureError(
            f"controller did not reach PROVIDER_EXITED; state={status.get('state')!r} "
            f"error={status.get('error')!r}"
        )
    if status.get("exit_code") != 0:
        raise FixtureError(
            f"provider exit code {status.get('exit_code')!r} is not 0; "
            f"stderr_path={status.get('stderr_path')!r}"
        )
    outcome = status.get("provider_terminal_outcome")
    if outcome != "COMPLETED":
        raise FixtureError(
            f"provider terminal outcome {outcome!r} is not COMPLETED"
        )
    session_id = status.get("provider_session_id")
    if not isinstance(session_id, str) or not session_id.strip():
        raise FixtureError(
            f"provider_session_id was not recorded: {session_id!r}"
        )

    events = _lane_events(runtime)
    # Lane event rows carry the event name under ``event`` (see lane_controller
    # ``_event``), not ``type``; the claude stream-json lines use ``type``.
    event_types = [row.get("event") for row in events]
    if "PROVIDER_STARTED" not in event_types or "PROVIDER_EXITED" not in event_types:
        raise FixtureError(
            f"lane event log is missing PROVIDER_STARTED/PROVIDER_EXITED: {event_types}"
        )
    started = next(row for row in events if row.get("event") == "PROVIDER_STARTED")
    exited = next(row for row in events if row.get("event") == "PROVIDER_EXITED")
    if not isinstance(started.get("provider_pid"), int):
        raise FixtureError(f"PROVIDER_STARTED has no provider_pid: {started}")
    if exited.get("provider_terminal_outcome") != "COMPLETED":
        raise FixtureError(f"PROVIDER_EXITED outcome wrong: {exited}")
    if exited.get("session_id") != session_id:
        raise FixtureError(
            "PROVIDER_EXITED session_id does not match the recorded provider_session_id"
        )

    # The real artifact: the model must have created and committed HELLO.txt.
    # Models write the fixed content with or without a trailing newline
    # (echo-style writes append one), so compare the stripped content.
    hello = lane / "HELLO.txt"
    if not hello.is_file():
        raise FixtureError("claude lane did not create HELLO.txt")
    hello_text = hello.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if hello_text.strip() != "hello from claude":
        raise FixtureError(
            f"HELLO.txt content is not the fixed fixture content: {hello_text!r}"
        )
    head = _git(lane, "rev-parse", "HEAD")
    if head == base_commit:
        raise FixtureError("claude lane made no commit")
    commit_count = int(_git(project, "rev-list", "--count", f"{base_commit}..{head}"))
    if commit_count < 1:
        raise FixtureError("HELLO.txt was not committed by the claude lane")

    return {
        "schema": "orchestrator-disposable-claude-fixture/v1",
        "provider_id": "claude-code",
        "model": CLAUDE_MODEL,
        "config_overrides": [CLAUDE_OLLAMA_OVERRIDE],
        "terminal_state": status.get("state"),
        "provider_terminal_outcome": outcome,
        "provider_exit_code": status.get("exit_code"),
        "provider_session_id": session_id,
        "provider_pid": started.get("provider_pid"),
        "base_commit": base_commit,
        "head_commit": head,
        "commit_count": commit_count,
        "hello_content": hello_text,
        "lane_event_count": len(events),
        "lane_event_types": event_types,
    }


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
    keep_root: Path | None = None
    if args:
        if len(args) != 2 or args[0] != "--keep":
            print(
                "usage: disposable_claude_coding_fixture.py [--keep DIRECTORY]",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2
        keep_root = Path(args[1]).resolve()
        if keep_root.exists():
            print("--keep DIRECTORY must not already exist", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        keep_root.mkdir(parents=True)
    try:
        if keep_root is not None:
            result = run_fixture(keep_root)
            result["cleanup"] = "retained by --keep"
        else:
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(
                prefix="orchestrator-claude-fixture-"
            ) as temporary:
                temporary_path = Path(temporary)
                result = run_fixture(temporary_path)
            result["cleanup"] = "temporary repository removed"
        print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, sort_keys=True))
        return 0
    except (FixtureError, OSError, ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        if keep_root is not None:
            print(f"fixture failed; retained at {keep_root}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        else:
            print(f"fixture failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

+def claude_config_override_env(override: str) -> Mapping[str, str]:
+    """Translate one claude-code ``config_overrides`` entry into env assignments.

1	"""Claude Code CLI compatibility tests for the WIP target harness.
2	
3	Tests the ``orchestrator_harness`` machinery with the ``claude-code`` provider
4	adapter (the stock adapter from ``provider.py`` plus a local ``FixedClaudeAdapter``
5	workaround subclass registered under ``claude-code-fixed``).  A fake CLI emits the
6	exact Claude Code stream-JSON protocol (``system/init`` -> STARTED,
7	``result/subtype:success`` -> COMPLETED, ``result/is_error:true`` -> FAILED) so the
8	deterministic tests never depend on the external model service.  A small number of
9	live tests launch the REAL ``claude`` CLI routed to the local Ollama
10	Anthropic-compatible endpoint (deepseek-v4-flash:0731-cloud) exactly as
11	``missing_claude_implementation.md`` prescribes.
12	
13	The four known claude-code gaps from ``missing_claude_implementation.md`` are
14	asserted here (they reproduce at the current commit), and the workaround adapter is
15	the test-only vehicle that lets every other feature be exercised for claude-code.
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import hashlib

69	
70	
71	class FixedClaudeAdapter(BaseProviderAdapter):
72	    """Stock ``ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter`` plus the two flags the real CLI needs.
73	
74	    1. ``--verbose`` (bug #1 in ``missing_claude_implementation.md``): the real
75	       Claude CLI hard-rejects ``--print --output-format stream-json`` without
76	       ``--verbose``.
77	    2. Default permission bypass (bug #2): Codex's adapter bypasses
78	       unconditionally; the stock claude adapter only bypasses when
79	       ``provider.permission_mode`` is explicitly set.  This subclass makes the
80	       bypass unconditional (mirroring codex) so a lane cannot silently
81	       false-COMPLETE because an optional field was omitted.
82	    """
83	
84	    provider_id = CLAUDE_TEST_PROVIDER_ID
85	
86	    def build_argv(self, spec: ProviderLaunchSpec) -> list[str]:
87	        from orchestrator_harness.provider import ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter
88	
89	        stock = ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter()
90	        argv = stock.build_argv(spec)
91	        if "--verbose" not in argv:
92	            argv.append("--verbose")
93	        if "--permission-mode" not in argv:
94	            argv.extend(["--permission-mode", "bypassPermissions"])
95	        return argv
96	
97	    def encode_prompt(self, prompt: bytes) -> bytes:
98	        from orchestrator_harness.provider import ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter
99	
100	        return ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter().encode_prompt(prompt)
101	
102	    def parse_transcript_line(self, line: bytes) -> ProviderEvent | None:
103	        from orchestrator_harness.provider import ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter
104

288	# Minimal stdio MCP server (newline-delimited JSON-RPC) that logs every request
289	# method to ``$MCP_LOG`` and answers ``initialize``/``tools/list``/``tools/call``.
290	# Used by the live claude+ollama MCP attempt: the boundary under test is whether
291	# the real claude CLI actually contacts the MCP server when launched with
292	# ``--mcp-config`` from the claude adapter's argv.
293	MCP_ECHO_SERVER = r"""
294	import json, os, sys
295	log_path = os.environ.get("MCP_LOG")
296	def log(msg):
297	    if log_path:
298	        try:
299	            with open(log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
300	                f.write(msg + "\n")
301	        except OSError:
302	            pass
303	for line in sys.stdin:
304	    line = line.strip()
305	    if not line:
306	        continue
307	    try:
308	        req = json.loads(line)
309	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
310	        continue
311	    method = req.get("method")
312	    rid = req.get("id")
313	    log("METHOD:" + str(method))
314	    if method == "initialize":
315	        out = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": rid, "result": {
316	            "protocolVersion": "2024-11-05",
317	            "capabilities": {"tools": {}},
318	            "serverInfo": {"name": "echo-server", "version": "0.1.0"},
319	        }}
320	    elif method == "notifications/initialized":
321	        continue
322	    elif method == "tools/list":
323	        out = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": rid, "result": {"tools": [{
324	            "name": "echo",
325	            "description": "Echo back the supplied text",
326	            "inputSchema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"text": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["text"]},
327	        }]}}
328	    elif method == "tools/call":
329	        args = (req.get("params") or {}).get("arguments") or {}
330	        log("CALL:" + json.dumps(args))
331	        out = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": rid, "result": {"content": [
332	            {"type": "text", "text": "echo: " + str(args.get("text"))}], "isError": False}}
333	    else:
334	        out = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": rid, "error": {"code": -32601, "message": "unknown method " + str(method)}}
335	    print(json.dumps(out), flush=True)
336	"""

1262	        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout

"""Claude Code CLI compatibility tests for the WIP target harness.

Tests the ``orchestrator_harness`` machinery with the ``claude-code`` provider
adapter (the stock adapter from ``provider.py`` plus a local ``FixedClaudeAdapter``
workaround subclass registered under ``claude-code-fixed``).  A fake CLI emits the
exact Claude Code stream-JSON protocol (``system/init`` -> STARTED,
``result/subtype:success`` -> COMPLETED, ``result/is_error:true`` -> FAILED) so the
deterministic tests never depend on the external model service.  A small number of
live tests launch the REAL ``claude`` CLI routed to the local Ollama
Anthropic-compatible endpoint (deepseek-v4-flash:0731-cloud) exactly as
``missing_claude_implementation.md`` prescribes.

The four known claude-code gaps from ``missing_claude_implementation.md`` are
asserted here (they reproduce at the current commit), and the workaround adapter is
the test-only vehicle that lets every other feature be exercised for claude-code.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import orchestrator_harness.lane_controller as controller
from orchestrator_harness.invocation import (
    CANONICAL_INVOCATION_SCHEMA,
    parse_canonical_invocation,
)
from orchestrator_harness.models import iso_utc
from orchestrator_harness.notifications import ManagerEventRouter
from orchestrator_harness.operator_launch import launch_process
from orchestrator_harness.processes import targeted_process_query
from orchestrator_harness.profile import RuntimeProfile
from orchestrator_harness.provider import (
    NOTIFICATION_MODE_SAFE_BOUNDARY_ONLY,
    BaseProviderAdapter,
    ProviderAdapterError,
    ProviderCapabilities,
    ProviderEvent,
    ProviderLaunchSpec,
    build_provider_evidence,
    classify_operation,
    decide_resume_or_handoff,
    notification_mode,
    provider_adapter,
    provider_config_digest,
    provider_registry,
    redact_command,
    register_provider_adapter,
    unregister_provider_adapter,
)
from orchestrator_harness.prompt_bundle import prompt_bundle_record_from_paths
from orchestrator_harness.task import TASK_CARD_SCHEMA, record_sha256
from orchestrator_harness.workspace_overlay import (
    SUPER_CACHE_NAME,
    ingest_super_cache,
    prepare_worktree,
)

CLAUDE_TEST_PROVIDER_ID = "claude-code-fixed"
CLAUDE_TEST_MODEL = "deepseek-v4-flash:0731-cloud"


class FixedClaudeAdapter(BaseProviderAdapter):
    """Stock ``ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter`` plus the two flags the real CLI needs.

    1. ``--verbose`` (bug #1 in ``missing_claude_implementation.md``): the real
       Claude CLI hard-rejects ``--print --output-format stream-json`` without
       ``--verbose``.
    2. Default permission bypass (bug #2): Codex's adapter bypasses
       unconditionally; the stock claude adapter only bypasses when
       ``provider.permission_mode`` is explicitly set.  This subclass makes the
       bypass unconditional (mirroring codex) so a lane cannot silently
       false-COMPLETE because an optional field was omitted.
    """

    provider_id = CLAUDE_TEST_PROVIDER_ID

    def build_argv(self, spec: ProviderLaunchSpec) -> list[str]:
        from orchestrator_harness.provider import ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter

        stock = ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter()
        argv = stock.build_argv(spec)
        if "--verbose" not in argv:
            argv.append("--verbose")
        if "--permission-mode" not in argv:
            argv.extend(["--permission-mode", "bypassPermissions"])
        return argv

    def encode_prompt(self, prompt: bytes) -> bytes:
        from orchestrator_harness.provider import ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter

        return ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter().encode_prompt(prompt)

    def parse_transcript_line(self, line: bytes) -> ProviderEvent | None:
        from orchestrator_harness.provider import ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter

        return ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter().parse_transcript_line(line)

    def terminal_outcome(self, event: ProviderEvent | None, exit_code: int) -> str:
        from orchestrator_harness.provider import ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter

        return ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter().terminal_outcome(event, exit_code)

    def redact_argv(self, argv: list[str] | tuple[str, ...]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        from orchestrator_harness.provider import ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter

        return ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter().redact_argv(argv)


def _load_stock_claude_adapter() -> Any:
    from orchestrator_harness.provider import ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter

    return ClaudeCodeProviderAdapter()


def _register_claude() -> None:
    """Register exactly the adapters this test module needs, once per process."""
    if "claude-code" not in provider_registry():
        register_provider_adapter(
            "claude-code",
            _load_stock_claude_adapter(),
            version="claude-code-v1",
            capabilities=ProviderCapabilities(
                launch=True,
                prompt=True,
                event_result=True,
                session=True,
                resume=True,
                permission=True,
                configuration=True,
                notification=False,
            ),
        )
    if CLAUDE_TEST_PROVIDER_ID not in provider_registry():
        register_provider_adapter(
            CLAUDE_TEST_PROVIDER_ID,
            FixedClaudeAdapter(),
            version="claude-code-fixed-v1",
            capabilities=ProviderCapabilities(
                launch=True,
                prompt=True,
                event_result=True,
                session=True,
                resume=True,
                permission=True,
                configuration=True,
                notification=False,
            ),
        )


# Fake CLI emitting the exact Claude Code stream-json protocol.
CLAUDE_FAKE_CLI = r"""

from pathlib import Path
argv = sys.argv[1:]
lane = argv[0]
delay = float(argv[1])
worker_invocation_id = argv[2] if len(argv) > 2 else f"{lane}-001"
emit_result = len(argv) <= 3 or argv[3] == "write-result"
release_signal = Path(argv[4]) if len(argv) > 4 and argv[4] != "-" else None
mode = argv[5] if len(argv) > 5 else "success"
sys.stdin.read()
print(json.dumps({"type": "system", "subtype": "init", "session_id": f"claude-{lane}"}), flush=True)
workspace = Path.cwd() / ".agent-workspace"

(workspace / "PARALLEL_CHECKPOINT.md").write_text(f"# {lane} checkpoint\n\nClaude worker started.\n", encoding="utf-8")
if release_signal is not None:
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 120
    while not release_signal.is_file():
        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
            raise SystemExit(3)
        time.sleep(0.05)
time.sleep(delay)
if lane in {"alpha", "beta", "beta-success"}:
    value = 1 if lane == "alpha" else 2
    feature_lane = "alpha" if lane == "alpha" else "beta"
    feature = Path.cwd() / f"feature_{feature_lane}.py"
    content = f"def value() -> int:\n    return {value}\n"
    if not feature.exists() or feature.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != content:

elif lane == "merge":

    branch = subprocess.run(["git", "branch", "--show-current"], cwd=Path.cwd(), capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    commit = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=Path.cwd(), capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    invocation = json.loads((workspace / f"{lane}.invocation.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    task_card = invocation["task_card"]
    result = {
        "schema": "orchestrator-task-result/v1",
        "card_id": task_card["id"],
        "lane_id": lane,
        "worker_invocation_id": worker_invocation_id,
        "cohort_id": invocation["cohort_id"],
        "revision": task_card["revision"],
        "task_card_sha256": task_card["sha256"],
        "prompt_bundle_sha256": invocation["prompt_bundle"]["bundle_sha256"],
        "prompt_content_sha256": invocation["prompt_bundle"]["final_sha256"],
        "branch": branch,
        "commit": commit,
        "outcome": "PASS",
        "summary": f"{lane} claude fixture work passed",
        "checks": [{"name": "fixture Python tests", "command": "python -m unittest -v", "outcome": "PASS"}],
    }
    (workspace / "RESULT.json").write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
if mode == "permission-denied":
    print(json.dumps({"type": "system", "subtype": "permission_denied", "tool_name": "Write"}), flush=True)
if mode == "error":
    print(json.dumps({"type": "result", "subtype": "error", "session_id": f"claude-{lane}", "is_error": True}), flush=True)
else:
    print(json.dumps({"type": "result", "subtype": "success", "session_id": f"claude-{lane}"}), flush=True)
"""


# Fake CLI emitting the exact Codex exec stream-json protocol so a codex lane can

CODEX_FAKE_CLI = r"""

"""


# Minimal stdio MCP server (newline-delimited JSON-RPC) that logs every request
# method to ``$MCP_LOG`` and answers ``initialize``/``tools/list``/``tools/call``.
# Used by the live claude+ollama MCP attempt: the boundary under test is whether
# the real claude CLI actually contacts the MCP server when launched with
# ``--mcp-config`` from the claude adapter's argv.
MCP_ECHO_SERVER = r"""
import json, os, sys
log_path = os.environ.get("MCP_LOG")
def log(msg):
    if log_path:
        try:
            with open(log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(msg + "\n")
        except OSError:
            pass
for line in sys.stdin:
    line = line.strip()
    if not line:
        continue
    try:
        req = json.loads(line)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        continue
    method = req.get("method")
    rid = req.get("id")
    log("METHOD:" + str(method))
    if method == "initialize":
        out = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": rid, "result": {
            "protocolVersion": "2024-11-05",
            "capabilities": {"tools": {}},
            "serverInfo": {"name": "echo-server", "version": "0.1.0"},
        }}
    elif method == "notifications/initialized":
        continue
    elif method == "tools/list":
        out = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": rid, "result": {"tools": [{
            "name": "echo",
            "description": "Echo back the supplied text",
            "inputSchema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"text": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["text"]},
        }]}}
    elif method == "tools/call":
        args = (req.get("params") or {}).get("arguments") or {}
        log("CALL:" + json.dumps(args))
        out = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": rid, "result": {"content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "echo: " + str(args.get("text"))}], "isError": False}}
    else:
        out = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": rid, "error": {"code": -32601, "message": "unknown method " + str(method)}}
    print(json.dumps(out), flush=True)
"""


def _git(cwd: Path, *args: str) -> str:
    completed = subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args],
        cwd=cwd,
        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        capture_output=True,
        check=True,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        errors="replace",
    )
    return completed.stdout.strip()


def _write_json(path: Path, value: object) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def _canonical(
    *,
    run: Path,
    runtime: Path,
    lane: str,
    worker_invocation_id: str,
    command: list[str],
    resources: list[str],
    provider_id: str = CLAUDE_TEST_PROVIDER_ID,
    model: str = CLAUDE_TEST_MODEL,
    overlay_receipt: Path | None = None,
    resume_identity: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    config_overrides: list[str] | None = None,
    mcp_config: object | None = None,
    provider_needs: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
    prompt_text: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    workspace = run / ".agent-workspace"
    workspace.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prompt = workspace / "worker-prompt.md"
    prompt.write_text(
        prompt_text or f"Complete the disposable {lane} claude lane.\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

        "schema": TASK_CARD_SCHEMA,
        "card_id": f"card-{lane}",
        "lane_id": lane,
        "stage_cohort_id": f"cohort-{lane}",
        "worker_invocation_id": worker_invocation_id,
        "objective": f"Do the bounded {lane} task",
        "revision": "r1",
    }
    profile = RuntimeProfile(
        f"profile-{lane}",
        "implementer",
        provider_id,
        model,
        ("Read", "Write", "Edit"),
        ("repo",),
        tuple(resources),
        provider_needs or ("CLAUDE_TEST",),
        ("WORKFLOW_TEST_FLAG",),
    )
    bundle = prompt_bundle_record_from_paths(
        workflow_id="workflow-1",
        task_card_id=f"card-{lane}",
        profile_id=f"profile-{lane}",
        paths=(("task", prompt),),
        run_root=run,
    )
    branch = _git(run, "branch", "--show-current")
    common_dir_value = _git(run, "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
    common_dir_path = Path(common_dir_value)
    common_dir = (
        (run / common_dir_path).resolve()
        if not common_dir_path.is_absolute()
        else common_dir_path.resolve()
    )
    value: dict[str, object] = {
        "schema": CANONICAL_INVOCATION_SCHEMA,
        "action": "start",
        "run_root": str(run),
        "runtime_root": str(runtime),
        "lane_id": lane,
        "worker_invocation_id": worker_invocation_id,
        "cohort_id": f"cohort-{lane}",
        "workflow": {"id": "workflow-1", "version": "1"},
        "task_card": {
            "id": f"card-{lane}",
            "revision": "r1",
            "sha256": record_sha256(card),
        },
        "role": "implementer",
        "provider": {
            "id": provider_id,
            "model": model,
            "command": command,
            "reasoning_effort": "high",
            "service_tier": "none",
            "sandbox": "danger-full-access",
            "approval_policy": "never",
            "config_overrides": config_overrides or [],
        },
        "profile": profile.to_record(),
        "prompt_bundle": bundle,
        "output_paths": {
            "status": str(workspace / f"{lane}_controller.status.json"),
            "jsonl": str(workspace / f"{lane}_provider.jsonl"),
            "stderr": str(workspace / f"{lane}.stderr.log"),
            "last_message": str(workspace / f"{lane}.last-message"),
        },
        "event_log_path": str(runtime / "events.jsonl"),
        "resources": resources,
        "repository": {
            "common_dir": str(common_dir),
            "worktree_root": str(run.resolve()),
            "branch": branch,
            "base_commit": _git(run, "rev-parse", "HEAD"),
        },
    }
    if overlay_receipt is not None:
        value["overlay_receipt"] = str(overlay_receipt)
    if resume_identity is not None:
        value["resume_identity"] = resume_identity
    if mcp_config is not None:
        value["provider"]["mcp_config"] = mcp_config
    return value


def _spec(
    *,
    action: str = "start",

    model: str = CLAUDE_TEST_MODEL,

        service_tier="standard",
        session_id=session_id,
        run_root=run_root or Path.cwd(),

class KnownClaudeGapsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """The four known claude-code gaps reproduce at the current commit."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        _register_claude()

    def test_gap1_stock_build_argv_missing_verbose(self) -> None:
        adapter = provider_adapter("claude-code")
        argv = adapter.build_argv(_spec())
        self.assertIn("--print", argv)
        self.assertIn("--output-format", argv)
        self.assertNotIn("--verbose", argv)
        # The real CLI rejects this exact combination (missing --verbose).
        self.assertIn("stream-json", argv)

    def test_gap1_fixed_adapter_adds_verbose(self) -> None:
        adapter = provider_adapter(CLAUDE_TEST_PROVIDER_ID)
        argv = adapter.build_argv(_spec())
        self.assertIn("--verbose", argv)
        self.assertIn("--permission-mode", argv)

    def test_gap2_stock_adapter_omits_bypass_without_field(self) -> None:
        adapter = provider_adapter("claude-code")
        argv = adapter.build_argv(_spec())
        self.assertNotIn("--permission-mode", argv)
        # With the field set, the bypass is emitted.
        spec = _spec()
        argv2 = adapter.build_argv(
            ProviderLaunchSpec(
                action="start", command=("claude",), model=CLAUDE_TEST_MODEL,
                reasoning_effort="medium", service_tier="standard", session_id=None,
                run_root=Path.cwd(), last_message_path=Path.cwd() / "lm",
                permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
            )
        )
        self.assertIn("--permission-mode", argv2)
        self.assertIn("bypassPermissions", argv2)

    def test_gap2_silent_false_completed_without_bypass(self) -> None:
        # The stock parse_transcript_line classifies permission-denied + success
        # as COMPLETED even though the requested work was never done.  This is
        # the silent-false-COMPLETED risk when permission_mode is omitted.
        adapter = provider_adapter("claude-code")
        denied = adapter.parse_transcript_line(
            b'{"type":"system","subtype":"permission_denied","tool_name":"Write"}'
        )
        self.assertIsNone(denied)  # permission_denied is not even classified
        success = adapter.parse_transcript_line(
            b'{"type":"result","subtype":"success"}'
        )
        self.assertEqual("COMPLETED", adapter.terminal_outcome(success, 0))

    def test_gap3_override_fields_accepted_then_dropped(self) -> None:
        adapter = provider_adapter(CLAUDE_TEST_PROVIDER_ID)
        spec = ProviderLaunchSpec(
            action="start", command=("claude",), model=CLAUDE_TEST_MODEL,
            reasoning_effort="medium", service_tier="standard", session_id=None,
            run_root=Path.cwd(), last_message_path=Path.cwd() / "lm",
            config_overrides=('model_provider="ollama"',),
            approval_policy="never",
            permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
            mcp_config={"mcpServers": {}},
        )
        argv = adapter.build_argv(spec)
        self.assertNotIn("model_provider", " ".join(argv))
        self.assertNotIn("--approval-policy", argv)
        self.assertIn("--permission-mode", argv)

    def test_gap4_no_claude_example_fixture_exists(self) -> None:
        examples = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "examples"
        self.assertTrue(examples.is_dir())
        names = [p.name for p in examples.iterdir()]
        self.assertFalse(any("claude" in n for n in names))

        _git(self.run, "config", "user.name", "Claude Tests")
        (self.run / "x.txt").write_text("x\n", encoding="utf-8")
        _git(self.run, "add", "x.txt")
        _git(self.run, "commit", "-m", "init")

        self.temporary.cleanup()

    def _inv(self, **overrides: object) -> dict[str, object]:
        value = _canonical(
            run=self.run,
            runtime=self.runtime,

            worker_invocation_id="alpha-001",
            command=[sys.executable, "claude"],
            resources=[],
        )
        value.update(overrides)
        return value

    def test_action_start_accepted(self) -> None:
        inv = parse_canonical_invocation(self._inv())
        self.assertEqual("start", inv.action)

    def test_action_unknown_rejected(self) -> None:
        raw = self._inv()
        raw["action"] = "frobnicate"
        with self.assertRaises(Exception):
            parse_canonical_invocation(raw)

    def test_resume_requires_session_identity(self) -> None:
        raw = self._inv()
        raw["action"] = "resume"
        raw["resume"] = {"session_id": "s-1"}
        inv = parse_canonical_invocation(raw)
        self.assertEqual("resume", inv.action)

    def test_start_cannot_contain_resume_block(self) -> None:
        raw = self._inv()
        raw["resume"] = {"session_id": "s-1"}
        with self.assertRaises(Exception) as ctx:
            parse_canonical_invocation(raw)
        self.assertIn("cannot contain resume", str(ctx.exception))

    def test_provider_notification_must_be_boolean(self) -> None:
        raw = self._inv()
        raw["provider"] = {**raw["provider"], "notification": "yes"}  # type: ignore[index]
        with self.assertRaises(Exception):
            parse_canonical_invocation(raw)

    def test_profile_role_must_match_invocation(self) -> None:
        raw = self._inv()
        raw["role"] = "reviewer"  # mismatches profile.role (implementer)
        with self.assertRaises(Exception):
            parse_canonical_invocation(raw)

    def test_profile_provider_must_match(self) -> None:
        raw = self._inv()
        raw["profile"] = {**raw["profile"], "provider_id": "codex"}  # type: ignore[index]
        with self.assertRaises(Exception):
            parse_canonical_invocation(raw)

    def test_unregistered_provider_rejected(self) -> None:
        raw = self._inv()
        raw["provider"] = {**raw["provider"], "id": "not-a-provider"}  # type: ignore[index]
        with self.assertRaises(Exception) as ctx:
            parse_canonical_invocation(raw)
        self.assertIn("not a registered provider", str(ctx.exception))

    def test_sha256_hex_digest_validation(self) -> None:
        raw = self._inv()
        raw["task_card"] = {**raw["task_card"], "sha256": "not-a-hex-digest"}  # type: ignore[index]
        with self.assertRaises(Exception):
            parse_canonical_invocation(raw)

    def test_string_list_no_duplicates(self) -> None:
        raw = self._inv()
        raw["resources"] = ["service:db", "service:db"]
        with self.assertRaises(Exception):
            parse_canonical_invocation(raw)

    def test_repository_worktree_matches_run_root(self) -> None:
        # The parse layer accepts the repository block; the git-safety layer
        # rejects a worktree_root that does not equal run_root.
        from orchestrator_harness.git_safety import (
            GitSafetyError,
            declaration_from_invocation,
        )

        raw = self._inv()
        other = self.root / "elsewhere"
        other.mkdir()
        raw["repository"] = {**raw["repository"], "worktree_root": str(other)}  # type: ignore[index]
        with self.assertRaises(GitSafetyError) as ctx:
            declaration_from_invocation(raw, self.run)
        self.assertIn("must equal run_root", str(ctx.exception))

    def test_canonical_output_paths_nonempty_string(self) -> None:
        raw = self._inv()
        raw["output_paths"] = {**raw["output_paths"], "status": ""}  # type: ignore[index]
        with self.assertRaises(Exception):

    def _start_async(
        self,
        run: Path,
        lane: str,
        worker_id: str,
        resources: list[str],
        command: list[str],
        provider_id: str = CLAUDE_TEST_PROVIDER_ID,
        config_overrides: list[str] | None = None,
        mcp_config: object | None = None,
        provider_needs: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
        prompt_text: str | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[Path, dict[str, Any]]:
        invocation = _canonical(
            run=run,
            runtime=self.runtime,
            lane=lane,
            worker_invocation_id=worker_id,
            command=command,
            resources=resources,
            provider_id=provider_id,

            provider_needs=provider_needs,

        )

        receipt = launch_process(

            label="lane-controller",

        )

    def _wait_for_status(
        self, run: Path, lane: str, predicate: Any, *, timeout: float = 180.0
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        import time

        path = run / ".agent-workspace" / f"{lane}_controller.status.json"
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            try:
                value = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
                time.sleep(0.05)
                continue
            if isinstance(value, dict) and predicate(value):
                return value
            time.sleep(0.05)
        raise AssertionError(f"timed out waiting for status condition in {path}")

    def _finish_async(self, receipt: dict[str, Any], run: Path, lane: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        import time

        pid = receipt.get("pid")
        created_utc = receipt.get("created_utc")
        self.assertIsInstance(pid, int)
        self.assertIsInstance(created_utc, str)
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 180.0
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            query = targeted_process_query(pid)
            if query.complete and not query.errors:
                process = query.process
                if process is None or iso_utc(process.created_utc) != created_utc:
                    return self._wait_for_status(
                        run,
                        lane,
                        lambda value: value.get("state")
                        in {"PROVIDER_EXITED", "CONTROLLER_FAILED", "LAUNCH_FAILED"},
                    )
            time.sleep(0.05)
        raise AssertionError(f"controller PID {pid} did not exit")

    def _status(self, run: Path, lane: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return json.loads(
            (run / ".agent-workspace" / f"{lane}_controller.status.json").read_text(
                encoding="utf-8"
            )
        )

        # Release alpha; beta proceeds.

class ClaudeCodexMixedTests(ClaudeMultiAgentTests):
    """V-section cross-CLI mixed-provider lanes: a claude-code-fixed lane and a
    codex lane run concurrently against the same project in one runtime, sharing
    one event log and one exclusive resource claim, driven through the real
    lane-controller launcher with the genuine adapters for both CLIs."""

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        super().setUp()
        self.codex_fake = self.root / "fake_codex.py"
        self.codex_fake.write_text(CODEX_FAKE_CLI, encoding="utf-8")

    def _codex_command(
        self, lane: str, delay: float, worker_id: str, emit: str, release: str
    ) -> list[str]:
        return [
            sys.executable,
            str(self.codex_fake),
            lane,
            str(delay),
            worker_id,
            emit,
            release,
        ]

    def test_mixed_claude_and_codex_lanes_share_event_log_and_locks(self) -> None:
        """A claude lane and a codex lane run concurrently in the same runtime;
        the shared resource claim serializes them, and the shared event log
        records both providers' lifecycle."""
        gamma = self.worktrees / "gamma"
        _git(
            self.project,
            "worktree",
            "add",
            "-b",
            "lane/gamma",
            str(gamma),
            self.base_commit,
        )
        alpha_release = self.runtime / "alpha-release.signal"
        _, alpha_receipt = self._start_async(
            self.alpha,
            "alpha",
            "alpha-001",
            ["service:mixed-db"],
            self._command("alpha", 0.0, "alpha-001", "write-result", str(alpha_release)),
        )
        self._wait_for_status(
            self.alpha,
            "alpha",
            lambda value: bool(value.get("held_resource_claims")),
        )
        _, codex_receipt = self._start_async(
            gamma,
            "gamma",
            "gamma-001",
            ["service:mixed-db"],
            self._codex_command("gamma", 0.0, "gamma-001", "write-result", "-"),
            provider_id="codex",
        )
        # The codex lane must wait on the same claim while the claude lane holds it.
        codex_waiting = self._wait_for_status(
            gamma,
            "gamma",
            lambda value: value.get("state") == "WAITING_RESOURCE",
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            "service:mixed-db", codex_waiting["waiting_resource_claim"]["resource"]
        )
        _write_json(alpha_release, {"release": True})
        alpha_status = self._finish_async(alpha_receipt, self.alpha, "alpha")
        self.assertEqual("PROVIDER_EXITED", alpha_status["state"])
        self.assertTrue(alpha_status["result_valid"])
        self.assertEqual("claude-code-fixed", alpha_status.get("provider_id"))
        codex_status = self._finish_async(codex_receipt, gamma, "gamma")
        self.assertEqual("PROVIDER_EXITED", codex_status["state"])
        self.assertTrue(codex_status["result_valid"])
        self.assertEqual("codex", codex_status.get("provider_id"))
        # The shared event log carries both providers' lifecycle records.
        events = [
            json.loads(line)
            for line in (self.runtime / "events.jsonl")
            .read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            .splitlines()
            if line.strip()
        ]
        started: dict[str, int] = {}
        for record in events:
            if record.get("event") == "PROVIDER_STARTED":
                started[record.get("provider_id")] = (
                    started.get(record.get("provider_id"), 0) + 1
                )
        self.assertIn("claude-code-fixed", started)
        self.assertIn("codex", started)
        # Each lane committed only on its own branch, and the codex lane's
        # feature file was actually materialized in its own worktree.
        self.assertEqual("lane/alpha", _git(self.alpha, "branch", "--show-current"))
        self.assertEqual("lane/gamma", _git(gamma, "branch", "--show-current"))
        self.assertTrue((self.alpha / "feature_alpha.py").exists())
        self.assertTrue((gamma / "feature_gamma.py").exists())

    def test_live_real_claude_and_codex_lanes_mixed_in_one_run(self) -> None:
        """LIVE cross-CLI test: the real ``claude`` CLI (routed to the local
        Ollama Anthropic endpoint) and the real ``codex`` CLI (routed to Ollama
        via provider overrides) run concurrently in the same runtime.  The
        assertion is on coordination — both lanes reach PROVIDER_EXITED and the
        shared event log records both providers — not on the model's result
        shape, so it tolerates model-service variance.  Skipped when either CLI
        or the local Ollama endpoint is unavailable."""
        import shutil
        import urllib.request

        if shutil.which("claude") is None or shutil.which("codex") is None:
            self.skipTest("real claude or codex CLI not on PATH")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(

    def test_live_claude_ollama_mcp_attempt(self) -> None:
        """LIVE MCP attempt, claude-code + Ollama only (codex excluded).

        The claude adapter maps the invocation's ``provider.mcp_config`` onto a
        ``--mcp-config`` argv flag, so this launches the REAL ``claude`` CLI (routed
        to Ollama) with a trivial stdio MCP echo server attached.  The boundary
        under test is whether the CLI actually contacts the MCP server when the
        lane is launched through the harness — a contacted server writes
        ``METHOD:initialize`` / ``METHOD:tools/list`` to its log.  This is the
        single documented MCP attempt; if the CLI never reaches the server the
        test fails and the boundary is recorded in the report."""
        import shutil
        import urllib.request

        if shutil.which("claude") is None:
            self.skipTest("real claude CLI not on PATH")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(
                "http://localhost:11434/api/tags", timeout=3
            ) as response:
                if response.status != 200:
                    raise OSError("ollama returned non-200")
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - environment dependent
            self.skipTest(f"local Ollama endpoint unavailable: {exc}")

        gamma = self.worktrees / "gamma"
        _git(
            self.project,
            "worktree",
            "add",
            "-b",
            "lane/gamma",
            str(gamma),
            self.base_commit,
        )
        server = self.root / "mcp_echo_server.py"
        server.write_text(MCP_ECHO_SERVER, encoding="utf-8")
        mcp_log = self.root / "mcp_server.log"
        config = self.root / "mcp.config.json"
        config.write_text(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    "mcpServers": {
                        "echo": {
                            "command": sys.executable,
                            "args": [str(server)],
                            "env": {"MCP_LOG": str(mcp_log)},
                        }
                    }
                }
            ),
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        # The harness child-environment isolation deliberately denies the
        # ANTHROPIC credential vars, but ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is grantable — declare
        # it in the profile so the real claude child actually routes to the local
        # Ollama endpoint instead of the (compute-less) Anthropic backend.
        env_keys = ("ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL", "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
        prior_env = {key: os.environ[key] for key in env_keys if key in os.environ}
        os.environ.update(
            {
                "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://localhost:11434",
                "ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN": "ollama",
                "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "",
            }
        )
        try:
            self._start(
                gamma,
                "gamma",
                "gamma-001",
                ["service:mcp-gamma-db"],
                ["claude"],
                mcp_config=str(config),
                provider_needs=("CLAUDE_TEST", "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"),
                prompt_text=(
                    "Do not modify any files. Call the mcp__echo__echo tool "
                    "exactly once with the text 'harness-mcp-probe'. Then reply "
                    "with the single word DONE and nothing else."
                ),
            )
            status = self._status(gamma, "gamma")
            self.assertEqual(
                "PROVIDER_EXITED",
                status["state"],
                f"claude lane did not exit cleanly: {status}",
            )
            self.assertEqual(
                "COMPLETED",
                status.get("provider_terminal_outcome"),
                f"claude provider did not complete: {status.get('provider_terminal_outcome')}",
            )
            try:
                methods = mcp_log.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
            except OSError:
                methods = []
            contacted = [line for line in methods if line.startswith("METHOD:")]
            self.assertTrue(
                contacted,
                "MCP server was never contacted by the claude CLI: "
                f"log {mcp_log} missing/empty; status={status}",
            )
            self.assertIn(
                "METHOD:initialize",
                contacted,
                f"MCP handshake missing; only saw {contacted}",
            )
            # tools/call is model-dependent (the model must choose to invoke the
            # echo tool), so it is reported, not required.
            called = [line for line in methods if line.startswith("CALL:")]
            if called:
                status["_mcp_called"] = called  # recorded for the report
        finally:
            for key in env_keys:
                if key in prior_env:
                    os.environ[key] = prior_env[key]
                else:
                    os.environ.pop(key, None)

def isolated_coding_child_environment(
    inherited: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
) -> tuple[dict[str, str], list[str]]:
    """Return the optional Codex-only child environment without physical lane capability."""
    source = dict(os.environ if inherited is None else inherited)
    cleared = sorted(
        key for key in source if key.upper().startswith(_PHYSICAL_CHILD_PREFIXES)
    )
    allowed = {
        key: value
        for key, value in source.items()
        if key.upper() in _CHILD_ENV_ALLOW
        and not key.upper().startswith(_PHYSICAL_CHILD_PREFIXES)
    }
    return allowed, cleared


def apply_provider_env_overrides(
    child_env: dict[str, str] | None,
    env_overrides: Mapping[str, str],
) -> dict[str, str] | None:
    """Merge declared provider env overrides AFTER isolation/allow-list filtering.

    Only the explicitly declared override keys pass; an override always wins
    over an inherited or allow-listed value.  With no isolation the child would
    have inherited the full parent environment anyway, so the merge starts from
    ``os.environ`` to avoid silently dropping PATH & friends.
    """
    if not env_overrides:
        return child_env
    merged = dict(os.environ) if child_env is None else dict(child_env)
    merged.update(env_overrides)
    return merged


def _atomic_json(path: Path, value: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    data = (json.dumps(value, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    try:
        mutation_replace(
            path.parent,
            path.name,
            data,
            expected=capture_target(path.parent, path.name),
        )
    except (MutationConflict, MutationUnsupported) as exc:
        raise OSError(str(exc)) from exc


def _append_event(path: Path, value: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    append_jsonl_record(path, value)

from __future__ import annotations

"""Thin public composition for launching one lane controller.

The operator launcher owns detached-process identity and receipt publication;
the lane controller owns invocation validation, provider launch, lifecycle,
claims, results, and cleanup.  This module only binds the two existing public
boundaries for examples and deterministic host-only journeys.
"""

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from .operator_launch import launch_process


def _default_controller_python() -> tuple[str, dict[str, str] | None]:
    """Return a non-redirecting Python command with the caller's import path.

    Windows virtual-environment ``python.exe`` launchers can redirect to the
    base interpreter in a second process. A detached receipt for the launcher
    would then identify the wrong process. Launch the detected base interpreter
    directly and carry forward the active import path so the receipt and
    controller status describe one exact process.
    """

    if os.name != "nt" or sys.prefix == sys.base_prefix:
        return sys.executable, None
    candidate = Path(sys.base_prefix) / Path(sys.executable).name
    try:
        executable = candidate.resolve(strict=True)
        current = Path(sys.executable).resolve(strict=True)
    except OSError:
        return sys.executable, None
    if executable == current or not executable.is_file():
        return sys.executable, None
    environment = dict(os.environ)
    import_paths = [value for value in sys.path if isinstance(value, str) and value]
    inherited = environment.get("PYTHONPATH")
    if inherited:
        import_paths.extend(value for value in inherited.split(os.pathsep) if value)
    environment["PYTHONPATH"] = os.pathsep.join(dict.fromkeys(import_paths))
    return str(executable), environment


def launch_lane_controller(
    invocation: str | Path,
    *,
    receipt: str | Path,
    cwd: str | Path,
    python_executable: str | None = None,
    label: str = "lane-controller",
    role: str = "coding-lane-controller",
    expected_state_path: str | Path | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Launch the supported lane-controller CLI through the operator boundary."""

    invocation_path = Path(invocation).expanduser().resolve(strict=True)
    if not invocation_path.is_file():
        raise ValueError(f"invocation must be a regular file: {invocation_path}")
    if python_executable is None:
        executable, environment = _default_controller_python()
    else:
        executable, environment = python_executable, None
    return launch_process(
        receipt=receipt,
        label=label,
        role=role,
        cwd=cwd,
        argv=(
            executable,
            "-m",
            "orchestrator_harness.lane_controller",
            str(invocation_path),
        ),
        expected_state_path=expected_state_path,
        environment=environment,
    )


__all__ = ["launch_lane_controller"]

    config: HarnessConfig,

    store = store_factory(config)

        config.watch_timeout_seconds if timeout_seconds is None else timeout_seconds
    )
    deadline = monotonic() + timeout
